title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-jamie-liu
content:
Goal: capture quick breadcrumbs from today's regional failover / smart-routing fallback incident. Personal notes / commands I ran, error snippets, hypotheses, and immediate next steps.

Summary:
- At ~2025-11-12T16:20:00Z we observed an elevated error-rate for requests routed to eu-west-2. Smart-routing started failing over traffic to secondary region (us-east-1) but a subset of requests continued to hit the original region causing client 5xx spikes. Fallback policy did not fully converge; some in-flight cache entries kept returning old routing decisions.

Timeline (local times converted to UTC):
- 16:18:12 - first spike in 5xx from eu-west-2 frontend (alerts fired).
- 16:19:05 - Canary health-checks for serving-pool-eu reported 40% fail rate.
- 16:20:00 - Smart-router started executing fallback policy (policy=regional-failover-v2). Logs show route selection falling back, but we see a prolonged tail of failures until 16:30:00.
- 16:31:12 - Manual override to force-route all traffic to us-east-1 mitigated errors.

Commands / queries I ran (copied):
- Check router logs (tail + grep):
  sudo journalctl -u smart-router -o cat --since "2025-11-12 16:00" | grep -E "fallback|route|policy" | tail -n 200
  => observed repeating lines like: "[2025-11-12T16:20:05Z] INFO fallback: policy=regional-failover-v2 selected target=us-east-1 for tenant=acct-123"
  but also these: "[2025-11-12T16:20:07Z] WARN route-selection: selected target=eu-west-2 (stale-cache) ttl_remaining=3s tenant=acct-456"

- Inspect routing cache (redis) keys:
  redis-cli -h redis-router-prd get router:tenant:acct-456:route
  => "eu-west-2|pool-3|v1"  (expected it to be us-east-1 after fallback)

- Force TTL dump:
  redis-cli -h redis-router-prd ttl router:tenant:acct-456:route
  => 2
  (we saw many keys with ttl <= 5s and some with ttl=0 but still returned results)

- Check health endpoints on serving nodes:
  curl -sS http://10.23.45.67:8080/health | jq .
  => {"status":"DEGRADED", "checks": {"gpu-temp": "ok", "kv-cache": "timeout"}}

- K8s checks for eu pool scaling & pods:
  kubectl -n serving get pods -l pool=eu-west-2 -o wide
  kubectl -n serving describe deployment serving-eu-pool-3
  => some pods in CrashLoopBackOff and several OOMKilled during the window (see pod logs).

- Extracted a typical request trace that failed after fallback initiated:
  TRACE id=trace-20251112-16-20-09 tenant=acct-456
    route_decision: eu-west-2 (cache_hit=true, cache_ttl=1s)
    fallback_checked: true (policy=regional-failover-v2)
    fallback_target: us-east-1 (chosen)
    connection_attempts: 1 -> connection to us-east-1 succeeded
    final: request still proxied to eu-west-2 due to upstream sticky-route header present
  => implication: older sticky-routing header prevented router from updating backend in-flight.

Error snippets observed:
- From router logs:
  ERROR [route-exec] unable to connect to instance (eu-west-2) err=connect_timeout
  WARN [cache] race on set-if-not-exists router:tenant:acct-456 (expected miss but found stale set)

- From serving node logs:
  panic: kv-cache timeout exceeded
  2025-11-12T16:19:57Z ERROR out-of-memory: container killed by OOMKiller

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) TTL granularity + race: routing cache uses very short TTLs (3-5s) and there's a race where the fallback path sets a new route but some in-flight requests still read the old key before the set completes; also race on set-if-not-exists leads to stale entries persisting.
2) Sticky-route propagation: downstream proxies (edge LB or tenant-specific proxy) may add a sticky header that instructs the router to honor the previous upstream; when fallback triggers, router honors header and client continues to be routed to failing region.
3) Health-check flapping + aggressive circuit breaker: health checks transiently failed during autoscale / pod restarts; fallback triggered, but controller didn't drain connections fast enough.
4) Partial configuration mismatch: policy version regional-failover-v2 has a bug where when cache_ttl < 5s it attempts optimistic updates that race with redis replication lag in eu cluster.

Evidence for hypothesis 1 & 2:
- Multiple 'stale-cache' WARNs in router logs with ttl_remaining <= 3s.
- Traces showing sticky-route header present (X-Redwood-Sticky: route=eu-west-2;ts=1699759207).
- Redis keys with low TTLs and occasional ttl=0 but still returning values.

Quick repro steps I tried:
- Locally simulated TTL race with redis: spin up small redis, run two processes where one sets key with NX and short TTL and the other reads in a tight loop. Repro: reader sees old value during window ~100-300ms.
- Simulated sticky header behavior by injecting X-Redwood-Sticky on requests to smart-router and observed router honoring it when header signature validated.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Forced override route map for affected tenant buckets to us-east-1 (manual write) and increased TTLs temporarily to 60s so fallback writes persist long enough.
- Scaled up eu pool nodes by +30% to reduce OOM churn (temporary).
- Adjusted health-check thresholds to debounce short failures (5 consecutive fails -> mark unhealthy).

Follow-ups / next actions:
- Engineering follow-up (serving-runtime + routing): add stronger atomic swap in redis for route update (SET key <new> PX 60000 and ensure replication ack or use redis WAIT). Evaluate trade-offs for latency.
- Validate sticky-header semantics: we need a policy to invalidate sticky header when fallback triggers (e.g., sign with fallback version id or set header ttl).
- Add a short window for in-flight drain: ensure router drains existing upstream connections for N seconds after marking pool unhealthy.
- Add more observability: histogram of cache_ttl at decision time, count of stale-cache events per tenant, per-policy.
- Create a reproducible integration test in staging that simulates ttl race with redis replication lag and verifies router behavior.

Notes / random thoughts:
- If redis replication lag is present in eu region (master->replica delay), short TTLs could exacerbate the problem when reads are served from replicas. Confirm whether router reads go to master or replica.
- Consider switching to a deterministic central authority for routing decisions for short windows (single-writer pattern) to avoid NX races.

Suggested owners:
- root cause + fix: Marcus Bell (serving-runtime) + Ethan Park (router infra)
- observability & alerting: Zoe Chen (eng-sre)
- policy + rollout: myself (Jamie Liu)

Linked tickets to file: JIRA-RWD-4521 (incident), JIRA-RWD-4523 (routing-cache-fix), JIRA-RWD-4524 (sticky-header-policy).

If I forget anything: key artifacts to save: full router logs for 16:00-16:40 UTC (s3 path), redis AOF snapshot during window, trace dumps for sampled traces where fallback executed but final request still hit eu-west-2.

End of breadcrumbs. Will flesh out a cleaner postmortem after sync with Marcus & Ethan.

-- Jamie
